body: Tuesday, June 30 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed held rates at its June meeting with a hawkish dot plot shift signaling higher-for-longer. The 10Y yield sits at 4.41% (−6 bps vs 4 weeks ago) while the 2Y has climbed to 4.10% (prior close, +12 bps vs 4W), compressing the 10Y-2Y spread to +28 bps, positive but still flat by historical standards — a flattening move that suggests the market is repricing the near-term path as more restrictive even as longer-duration bonds catch a modest bid. Margin debt is reportedly getting more expensive, per Reuters, adding friction to the levered bid. VIX at 16.63 (↑3.6% vs 4W) remains in complacency territory but is ticking up.

New / Most Important: The Supreme Court dominated social conversation with rulings on birthright citizenship and 14th Amendment interpretation, including references to Trump executive orders on visas. The June jobs report is the next macro catalyst this week. The BIS issued a pointed warning that AI exuberance risks a lengthy investment bust — this is the first time the "central bank of central banks" has explicitly used bubble language around AI capex. Bond spreads have narrowed (Yahoo), consistent with credit markets ignoring what the BIS is flagging.

Playbook ✓: Rotation from mega-cap tech into broader market is proceeding textbook — Russell 2000 at 3024.64 (↑4.1%) is outperforming Nasdaq 100 at 30282.88 (↓0.8%), with Russell/Nasdaq ratio ↑4.9%. Wharton's Siegel called this a sign of a healthier bull market. Dow hitting records while S&P 500 at 7497.42 (↓1.3%) lags confirms value/cyclical rotation.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The divergence is that credit spreads are narrowing INTO a hawkish dot-plot shift — typically spreads widen when the Fed signals prolonged restriction. This suggests either the credit market is pricing a soft landing with complete conviction, or — more likely from a capital-flows lens — foreign capital inflows into USD fixed income (attracted by dollar strength and yield pickup vs. Europe/Japan) are mechanically compressing spreads regardless of Fed rhetoric. The strong dollar narrative (DXY near 13-month highs per recent OCBC revisions) is pulling global savings into US credit, masking what should be tightening stress. Watch for this compression to reverse violently if the dollar peaks or if the jobs report this week shows labor market cracks.

Macro Stance: The ECB is in a policy limbo that is rapidly becoming a structural problem. Lagarde said the ECB doesn't need to fight inflation with "same force" as 2022-23, signaling comfort with the current stance. But ECB's Wunsch said another hike might be needed, Apollo's Slok flagged a possible September hike, and Bundesbank's Nagel warned inflation will stay "well above target." This is the most hawkish cacophony from the ECB in months.

New / Most Important: Flash inflation data from top eurozone economies showed slowing but remains above target — the Bundesbank's explicit warning that it stays "well above" is the critical signal. Lagarde simultaneously said Europe's economic resilience gives the ECB "greater room to move rates" — a constructive-sounding statement that actually opens the door to tightening, not easing. The euro is underperforming ahead of German HICP data, which is unusual if the market believed the easing narrative. This is a structurally important shift: the ECB consensus has flipped from "next move is a cut" to "next move could be a hike" in the span of two weeks. For cross-border flows, a hawkish ECB repricing narrows the US-EU rate differential, which should weaken USD/EUR — but the euro is falling anyway, suggesting capital is fleeing Europe on growth fears, not chasing yield. This creates a toxic combination: tighter money into a fragile growth environment. European bonds need close monitoring for a Q3 selloff.

Playbook ✓: Inflation stickiness in services sector continuing to frustrate policymakers — entirely on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Euro weakening despite hawkish ECB repricing is the key break — it means the capital flow story is dominating the rate differential story, which is bearish for European risk assets.

Macro Stance: The PBOC's new overnight framework is now live. After debuting the overnight reverse repo at 1.25% (Reuters, [Jun 28]), it doubled the overnight cash injection while keeping the rate unchanged (Reuters, [Jun 29]); Bloomberg notes the surprise that no rate was formally released ([Jun 29]). With loan prime rates still on hold, the easing is happening at the very front end and through volume, not through a headline cut. The yuan fixing was weakened for a fourth session as the dollar advanced (Bloomberg, [Jun 23]), a managed drift against a dollar near 13-month highs, while Euronews details how the currency widens the EU's deficit ([Jun 23]); T. Rowe Price sees the yuan 1%-2% weaker by year-end (TradingView, [Jun 26]). Prices are split: May CPI rose only 1.2% (China Daily, [Jun 10]) while factory-gate inflation hit a near four-year high (Reuters, [Jun 9]).

PMIs & Activity: The growth pulse turned up in June. The official manufacturing PMI rose to 50.3 (Reuters, [Jun 29]), back into expansion from a flat 50 in May (Reuters, [May 30]) and faster than expected on tech export demand (CNBC, [Jun 29]); the non-manufacturing PMI rose to 50.2 (Reuters, [Jun 29]). The composition matters: Bloomberg frames it as a return to growth because exports are booming ([Jun 29]), and ING still expects a second-quarter slowdown ([Jun 29]). The May hard data show why: industrial output growth quickened to 4.5% (China Daily, [Jun 16]), but retail sales fell 0.6%, the first drop in over three years (Il Sole 24 Ore, [Jun 15]), and fixed-asset investment was down 4.1% in the first five months (Macau Business, [Jun 16]). Industrial profits rose 18.8% in January–May (WSJ, [Jun 26]), but profit growth slowed for the first time in six months as weak domestic demand bit (Times of India, [Jun 27]).

Credit Impulse: Total social financing grew 7.7% in May (CGTN, [Jun 12]) and topped forecasts (Bloomberg, [Jun 12]), but new loans missed as the property slump curbed demand (Reuters, [Jun 12]). The beat is government-bond issuance; private credit demand is still contracting. The PBOC is now urging banks to boost lending because demand remains weak, according to sources (Reuters, [Jun 26]). Household deleveraging continues (SCMP, [Jun 15]). Read: the headline impulse is flat-to-positive, but the household and private-firm impulse is still negative, which is why output does not convert into consumption.

Property: New home prices fell at a faster pace in May (Reuters, [Jun 15]) even as first-tier new home prices rose for a third month (SCMP, [Jun 16]) and top-city resale prices extended their rebound (Caixin, [Jun 17]). Real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May (GMK Center, [Jun 18]). This week the stress resurfaced at the developer level: Beijing land sales plunged 66% as developers chase only "safe" prime plots (Caixin, [Jun 25]), and the Evergrande Property Services stake sale collapsed, sending its shares down 24% (Caixin, [Jun 26]). Nikkei Asia notes state developers are powering Shenzhen construction despite market woes ([Jun 29]): state capital replacing private developers.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal policy is tightening at the margin: Beijing narrowed its cumulative deficit for the first time since 2023 (Business Times, [Jun 23]), and the 62.5 billion yuan third batch of trade-in funds (Global Times, [Jun 26]) is small against the retail contraction. The State Council reviewed AI, trade and carbon plans (Dimsum Daily, [Jun 29]), with no new demand package. On trade, the EU and China agreed an October deadline to reset ties (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]), with three months of talks over a €360bn deficit (The Guardian, [Jun 29]) and a €3 customs charge on small parcels aimed at cheap Chinese imports (The Guardian, [Jun 29]). Beijing kept using export controls as leverage, adding 20 Japanese entities to its dual-use list (Reuters, [Jun 29]) after targeting US rare-earth firms (Mexico Business News, [Jun 24]). The NYT casts China as a relative winner from the Strait of Hormuz crisis ([Jun 29]).

Markets & Flows: Hong Kong rebounded to 23,026 on US-Iran peace-talk optimism and a tech recovery (BBN Times, [Jun 29]) after capping its worst week in over a year (SCMP, [Jun 26]), and broker stocks eye their best month since October on a trading boom (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]). But the relative picture is poor: Bloomberg says Chinese stocks are trailing the AI boom by the most since 2001 ([Jun 29]). Regulators are also clamping down on higher-yielding offshore debt issuance (Bloomberg, [Jun 29]), tightening one more outflow and funding channel.

New / Most Important: The June PMI is the first upturn in the growth pulse in months, and it is export-led. Manufacturing back above 50 on tech export demand, with services barely positive, fits the same split as May: an AI and export engine running hot while household demand and private credit stay weak. Paired with cheaper overnight money and the October EU deadline, the near-term risk for China is not recession but a trade backlash against the very sector that is carrying growth.

Playbook ✓: Property drag, weak consumption, LPR on hold and a managed yuan drift lower are all on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The consensus expected a mid-year stimulus pivot; instead the June PMI upturn rests on exports while the credit impulse outside government bonds is negative and the fiscal impulse is narrowing. China is therefore exporting its excess supply rather than absorbing it at home. The transmission runs through three channels. European exporters face a €360bn deficit and a weak yuan, which is why Brussels has set an October deadline. Bulk-commodity demand tied to construction is fading with the investment slump, a drag on AUD and iron ore that an export-led PMI does not offset. And global goods disinflation is the channel Pimco expects to support EM bonds (Bloomberg, [Jun 23]). A real turn needs loan growth, not bond issuance, to re-accelerate; until it does, rallies in Hong Kong are flows, not fundamentals.

Macro Stance: The yen has collapsed to a 39-40 year low, breaking 162/USD, and the BOJ just underwent what Reuters calls a "slow, dovish revamp" that casts doubt on any near-term rate hikes. Factory output has slipped. The US-Japan rate gap continues to underpin dollar strength and yen weakness.

New / Most Important: This is a structurally critical moment. The yen at 162 is uncharted territory for the post-Plaza Accord era and represents a regime break in Japanese capital flow dynamics. PM Takaichi's BOJ appointee urged "vigilance" on yen's inflation impact, but Tokyo is keeping its intervention powder dry, with the "line in the sand" apparently shifting higher. The BOJ's dovish personnel revamp makes a July hike increasingly unlikely, which means the carry trade is being re-endorsed by the institution itself. This has massive global implications: Japanese lifers and pension funds running unhedged foreign bond positions at these FX levels face mark-to-market gains that discourage repatriation — meaning Japanese capital stays deployed in US Treasuries and European credit, compressing yields globally. The paradox is that a weaker yen is globally reflationary (cheaper Japanese exports, costlier imports for Japan) while simultaneously acting as a liquidity injection into DM fixed income. If intervention does come, the snap-back in global yields could be severe as repatriation flows reverse.

Playbook ✓: Yen weakness on rate differentials is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The BOJ's dovish institutional revamp actively undermines its own stated normalization path — the central bank is being restructured to NOT hike, even as imported inflation surges. This is policy incoherence of the highest order.

Macro Stance: The RBA is maintaining a restrictive stance, with minutes signaling policy needs to stay tight. The RBA warned that union inflation expectations are too high and flagged weak productivity growth as a structural concern. Another rate hike is explicitly on the table.

New / Most Important: The RBA minutes revealed a central bank that is simultaneously worried about inflation (union expectations), considering hiking further, and preparing "fire drills" for the next crisis. The AUD is falling despite hawkish minutes — the same pattern as EUR — suggesting the strong USD is overwhelming local rate signals. Weak productivity growth is the structural issue: it means the RBA needs to keep rates higher for longer to achieve the same disinflationary effect, a painful equilibrium for an economy with high household leverage.

Playbook ✓: Hawkish hold with tightening bias is on-script for an economy with sticky services inflation and high housing costs.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: AUD falling despite hawkish RBA suggests China-linked demand weakness is dominating the terms-of-trade story — China's real-estate investment fell 16.2% y/y in January–May, its June PMI recovery is export-led rather than construction-led, and oil is ↓24.3% — making Australia a casualty of China's property slowdown regardless of domestic policy.

Macro Stance: The GUS flash reset the rate debate: June CPI fell to 2.5%, the NBP target, which Parkiet says finally kills the chance of hikes [Jun 30]; Rzeczpospolita notes inflation has not been this low since February [Jun 30] and Fakt credits fuel for the surprise [Jun 30]. ING's economists say the market may start playing for cuts in the second half of 2026 [Jun 30], TVN24 carries the same line [Jun 30], and Bankier.pl reports the market has withdrawn its bet on dearer credit [Jun 30], a sharp turn from a week in which NBP disclosed a vote for a hike (Tysol.pl, [Jun 22]). The caveats are immediate: Gazeta Prawna estimates the withdrawal of the CPN fuel package could push inflation back toward 3% [Jun 30], Bankier.pl expects inflation to jump again while the NBP stays calm [Jun 30], and Direct Money gives one reason not to celebrate early [Jun 30]. Domański acknowledged fuel prices will rise as CPN passes into history (Biznes Wprost, [Jun 30]). GUS also published its GDP release (Interia Biznes, [Jun 30]), and Business Insider Polska describes the economy's biggest weakness as a collision with a wall [Jun 30]. No new rate action this cycle, but the bias has shifted from hike risk to a cut debate.

Markets: The zloty did not read the data as good news: Business Insider Polska reports it unexpectedly losing on the print [Jun 30], Bankier.pl has the euro reaching 4.30 zł and the pound nearly 5 zł [Jun 30], and Comparic.pl sees losses deepening [Jun 30], with Next Gazeta.pl pointing to a strong dollar and a possible Japanese intervention [Jun 30]. The card, at Monday's close, shows USD/PLN at 3.7538 (+0.5% 1W, +3.2% 4W) and EUR/PLN at 4.2864 (+0.5% 1W, +1.2% 4W). Equities turned: KGHM recovered losses on Tuesday with Budimex and Kruk leading (Inwestycje.pl, [Jun 30]), PKO BP, PGE and Tauron were in focus on dividend news (FXMAG, [Jun 30]), CD Projekt rose as the company lifted the veil on new products (INNPoland.pl, [Jun 30]), while LPP fell even as analysts suggest buying (INNPoland.pl, [Jun 30]). Monday's closes: EPOL 38.48 (-2.2% 1W, -5.0% 4W); KGHM 321.0 (-12.8% 1W, -8.2% 4W); Orlen 125.0 (-2.0% 1W, -11.8% 4W); PGE 9.47 (-3.8% 1W, -10.5% 4W); Allegro 37.15 (-3.7% 1W, +6.8% 4W); CD Projekt 221.1 (-3.7% 1W); LPP 18500 (+0.8% 1W, -18.1% 4W); PKO 103.3 (-1.4% 1W); Pekao 227.5 (-1.7% 1W, -6.0% 4W); Dino 29.28 (+0.9% 1W). Bloomberg reports Poland's new retail investors are fuelling record stock sales by listed firms [Jun 30], and Play priced a 1.25 bn zł bond (White & Case, [Jun 30]). MF disclosed a surprisingly high level of cash buffers (Business Insider Polska, [Jun 30]).

Fiscal & Politics: wPolityce.pl reads the EU convergence report as giving Poland the worst public finances in the bloc [Jun 30], days after the same report said Poland is not ready for the euro (Reuters, [Jun 24]); Biznes Alert calculates the state takes 229 days of earnings a year [Jun 30]. The windfall tax now carries a Senate amendment allowing up to 100% of profit (Strefa Inwestorów, [Jun 29]). The Central Register of Contracts goes live at the start of July, letting anyone see officials' spending (Rzeczpospolita, [Jun 30]), and municipalities received millions more under the local-finance reform (INFOR.PL, [Jun 30]). Rzeczpospolita's call to review state spending [Jun 29] stands. The WIBOR exit is nearer, with banks obliged to make clients a new offer (Bankier.pl, [Jun 30]).

Corporate & Sectors: Energy is on alert: PSE declared a warning state and issued capacity-market calls (Rzeczpospolita, [Jun 30]), the de minimis deadline for capped power prices falls today (Gazeta Prawna, [Jun 30]), and the government is changing energy law to reshape bills (Polskie Radio 24, [Jun 30]). Nuclear moved from paper to site: work at the first plant begins in July (wnp.pl, [Jun 30]), the American partner opened a Gdańsk office (Urbanity, [Jun 30]) and a document finally shows who will not build the second plant (wnp.pl, [Jun 30]); Orlen and Synthos filed for an SMR contract for difference (GlobEnergia, [Jun 30]). Orlen raised wholesale fuel prices again (wnp.pl, [Jun 30]) and is now Lithuania's largest company (pb.pl, [Jun 30]). PKO BP's 6.14 zł dividend (Bankier.pl, [Jun 29]) anchors the bank story against a sector earning 13.3 bn zł under tax and margin pressure (CEO Magazyn, [Jun 29]). Housing is at an inflection: mortgage servicing cost has equalled rent (Bankier.pl, [Jun 30]), mortgage lending set new records (Rzeczpospolita, [Jun 30]) and creditworthiness is rising faster than prices (Business Insider Polska, [Jun 30]). CD Projekt released a new Edgerunners 2 trailer with the series due this year (CD PROJEKT RED, [Jun 30]).

Geopolitics & Security: The NATO summit in Ankara is imminent (World Socialist Web Site, [Jun 30]), with Poland's spy chief saying the country must act as if war with Russia were imminent (TVP World, [Jun 29]) and Decode39 reporting Russia's influence operations turning toward Poland [Jun 30]. The Dutch assessment that Russia could attack NATO a year after the Ukraine war ends (Kyiv Post, [Jun 29]) and the Saab submarine order worth 4.3 billion dollars (Investing.com, [Jun 29]) set the defence tone.

New / Most Important: Inflation at 2.5% is the week's pivot, but the market reaction is the lesson: the zloty fell on a target-consistent print because a cut debate at a time of 1.5 bn zł a day of borrowing (wPolityce.pl, [Jun 26]) and a 100% windfall-tax ceiling reads as fiscal dominance, not disinflation. With CPN gone and petrol at 6 zł (Rzeczpospolita, [Jun 29]), Gazeta Prawna's 3% path is the base case, so the cut bias is real but the first cut is a second-half story at best.  |  Playbook ✓: Shift from hold to cut bias; add duration on the print, keep PKO into the dividend, and use the KGHM rebound to lighten rather than add.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: CPI at target while the zloty weakens to 4.30 per euro; record retail-driven equity issuance against EPOL down 5.0% over four weeks; mortgage lending records as PSE declares a grid warning.

Macro Stance: The RBI warned that every rise in oil prices could hit India's economy. With WTI at 69.76 (↓24.3% vs 4W), the immediate oil shock risk has actually diminished sharply — this is net positive for India's current account.

New / Most Important: NSE and Jio Platforms IPOs are revealing signals about India's changing economy per BBC — domestic capital market deepening is a structural EM story. The oil collapse is a significant terms-of-trade tailwind for India, partially offset by strong USD headwinds.  |  Playbook ✓: India as the EM beneficiary of lower oil is on-script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: None today.

Narrative: The market reads the rotation out of mega-cap tech as healthy rather than systemic, with the Dow at records: the Nasdaq 100 at 30282.88 (↓0.8% vs 4W) lags small caps, and big tech faces AI spending scrutiny ahead of Q2 earnings (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 29]).

Reported: BlackBerry lifted its annual revenue forecast as the QNX unit powered growth (BNN Bloomberg, [Jun 25]); Q1 earnings exceeded expectations and the stock climbed 20% (TradingView, [Jun 26]). TD SYNNEX beat on Q2 revenue and analysts raised targets (scanx.trade, [Jun 25]). Accenture's revenue-growth guidance cut shocked the IT services industry (The Hindu, [Jun 27]).

EPS Upside Watch: Oracle — a $638 billion AI backlog (24/7 Wall St., [Jun 23]) is contracted revenue still to convert into earnings. IBM — shares jumped 5% after JPMorgan upgraded the stock on software acceleration (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 24]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The BIS warning that AI exuberance risks a lengthy investment bust gives large allocators institutional cover to trim AI exposure, and such warnings tend to precede informal prudential pressure on bank exposure. With credit spreads narrowing at the same time, that dissonance is likely to resolve sharply one way.
Narrative: The platforms are caught in the tech rotation, but engagement stays robust and Visa says AI and online shopping are propping up growth, which supports the digital-ad complex.
Reported: Prosus' profit got a boost from food delivery, travel bookings and Tencent (Business Day, [Jun 29]).

EPS Upside Watch: Take-Two — an analyst says GTA VI could transform earnings (Benzinga, [Jun 24]), a single-title step-up in revenue and margins. PLDT — a data center REIT is seen as a boon to the Philippine telecom's balance sheet (Inquirer.net, [Jun 23]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is usually framed as a tailwind for the ad platforms, but OpenAI now wants $100bn of ad revenue (The Media Leader, [Jun 25]) — a new rival competing for the same budgets.

Narrative: Narrowing bond spreads help bank credit books and a 2Y at 4.10% (+12 bps vs 4W) with a +28 bps curve supports net interest margins, while pricier margin lending lifts prime-brokerage revenue; credit quality is the swing factor, as Judo's bad loans show.

Reported: Jefferies' quarterly profit missed estimates as asset management weighed (Reuters, [Jun 24]), despite record investment-banking revenue (Quiver Quantitative, [Jun 25]). Australia's Judo Capital cut FY26 profit guidance after three loans went bad (Stocks Down Under, [Jun 25]) and the shares tanked (AFR, [Jun 25]).

EPS Upside Watch: Standard Chartered — upgraded by Deutsche Bank as the Asian wealth boom drives its earnings outlook (Yahoo Finance UK, [Jun 23]). Higher-for-longer US rates could also lift Singapore banks' earnings beyond 2026 (The Business Times, [Jun 25]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.

Narrative: WTI at 69.76 (↓24.3% vs 4W) is a supply-driven slide that cuts upstream earnings: US drillers added rigs for a fourth straight week and Iraq's push for a bigger OPEC quota (Reuters, [Jun 29]) points to more supply, not less.

Reported: ADNOC L&S sees stronger 2026 earnings after a shipping boost (Gulf News, [Jun 29]). Worley, the engineering contractor to the energy and resources industries, issued a fresh profit warning (AFR, [Jun 25]). Oil-tanker earnings plunged by $200,000 as more vessels returned to Hormuz (Bloomberg.com, [Jun 26]).

EPS Upside Watch: Big oil's trading arms — the majors' secretive trading desks are having an extraordinary year (The Economist, [Jun 28]), a profit source beyond upstream prices. Energy Transfer — the pipeline operator raised its 2026 guidance by $750 million (TIKR.com, [Jun 29]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: A 24% crude drop with rig counts rising four weeks running sets up an energy-equity capitulation, as producers' higher-priced hedges roll off and Q3 results reveal spot exposure to sub-70 crude. Healthy global trade volumes make it a buyable dip for patient capital, but only once the supply overhang clears.

Narrative: Industrials lead the cyclical rotation, with the Russell 2000 at 3024.64 (↑4.1%) and the Dow at records, and US retailers front-loading China orders for the holiday season (Reuters, [Jun 29]) keep freight volumes firm.

Reported: AeroVironment soared 28% on an earnings beat as its backlog grew to $1.2 billion (CNBC, [Jun 29]). Maersk raised profit guidance as new US tariffs fuel demand (Financial Times, [Jun 29]). FedEx beat revenue and earnings estimates yet the stock dipped 6% (TIKR.com, [Jun 24]) as it warned on inflation and trade turmoil (Bloomberg.com, [Jun 23]).

EPS Upside Watch: RTX — earns a Zacks Buy upgrade as earnings estimates climb (Foreign Policy Journal, [Jun 29]). Southwest Airlines — UBS raised its target to $61 on the earnings outlook (Investing.com, [Jun 23]), with cheaper fuel dropping to margins.
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.

Narrative: Cheaper fuel (WTI ↓24.3%) helps consumers, but a hawkish Fed and pricier margin lending cap sentiment, outlooks keep disappointing, and Nike's EPS and revenue estimate revisions are still moving lower into its report (Seeking Alpha, [Jun 29]).

Reported: Carnival beat earnings expectations and analysts now have new forecasts (Simply Wall Street, [Jun 29]), after the Iran war cut its cruise profit outlook (Tech Times, [Jun 24]). Darden beat but forecast annual profit below estimates on higher costs (BNN Bloomberg, [Jun 25]). Winnebago missed estimates but surged 14% after earnings (MarketBeat, [Jun 29]).

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon — AWS hiked GPU prices again (TIKR.com, [Jun 29]), pricing power on AI compute. Halfords — the UK retailer sees fiscal year 2027 profit near the top end of analyst estimates (Reuters, [Jun 25]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.
Narrative: Defensive and dividend-oriented flows in a hawkish hold favour staples, falling input and freight costs (WTI ↓24.3%) help margins, and McCormick's beat shows pricing power is intact.

Reported: McCormick topped profit estimates on higher pricing (Reuters, [Jun 25]) as organic sales grew (TradingView, [Jun 25]). Couche-Tard beat estimates on strong fuel margins (BNN Bloomberg, [Jun 23]), delivering its 'best performance in years' in the US, its CEO said (C-Store Dive, [Jun 24]).
EPS Upside Watch: None flagged; General Mills reports next (StockStory, [Jun 29]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.
Narrative: Defensives should draw flows as the VIX ticks up to 16.63, and small-cap biotech is getting sell-side attention, but a 10Y at 4.41% and a hawkish Fed keep a lid on multiples.
Reported: No major reports this week.

EPS Upside Watch: Hims — the cash-pay telehealth platform's obesity-drug business may get a boost as employers drop coverage (Reuters, [Jun 25]). Dr Reddy's — Nomura sees 35% upside after its strategic consumer-health pivot (The Financial Express, [Jun 23]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.

Narrative: Copper at 6.25 (↓4.2% vs 4W) trades as an AI data-centre and grid-capex metal and is sliding with gold at 4040.90 (↓9.7%), so the metals tape stays weak despite chemicals beats. In China, real-estate investment (−16.2% y/y in January–May) keeps construction materials weak.

Reported: Evonik raised its 2026 outlook (European Coatings, [Jun 29]) after a strong second-quarter earnings surge (Indian Chemical News, [Jun 27]), citing higher prices and cost reductions (WSJ, [Jun 26]). Harita Nickel posted stronger earnings on higher Q1 nickel sales volumes (Petromindo, [Jun 26]).
EPS Upside Watch: Satellite Chemical — forecasts first-half net profit surging over 118% to a record, as its ethane-based route crushes oil-based rivals on cost (finance.biggo.com, [Jun 23]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gold falling 9.7% in four weeks without a safe-haven bid points to forced liquidation to meet margin calls elsewhere, or a shift in its link to real rates. Central bank buying, which drove the prior rally, may be pausing as EM central banks defend their currencies against the strong dollar.

Narrative: A 10Y at 4.41% (−6 bps vs 4W) gives cap rates marginal relief, but the hawkish dot plot caps hopes of further easing and mortgage rates near 6.5% (Realtor.com, [Jun 25]) keep transaction volumes suppressed.

Reported: Tosei REIT's distribution hit a record ¥3,926 for a fourth straight term with rent increases at 90% of turnovers, though rate hikes will trim ¥100 next term (finance.biggo.com, [Jun 29]). KB Home's Q2 earnings met estimates (Yahoo Finance, [Jun 23]) and the stock jumped (The Motley Fool, [Jun 24]). UK homebuilder Berkeley's profit fell 15% (Reuters, [Jun 24]).

EPS Upside Watch: Industrial REITs — MBSB sees them benefiting from data centre spin-offs and acquisitions (EdgeProp, [Jun 24]). Axis REIT — analysts call its latest purchase earnings-accretive (The Edge Malaysia, [Jun 26]).
⚡ Breaking Convention: None today.

Narrative: AI data-centre power demand is the secular driver, defensive rotation adds support and lower natural gas costs help margins, while a bill moving in Congress would make tech companies pay those energy costs (CNBC, [Jun 24]).
Reported: UK multi-utility supplier Telecom Plus fell 25% on its profit outlook and a dividend cut (Sharecast.com, [Jun 23]).

EPS Upside Watch: Bloom Energy — the supplier of on-site fuel-cell power to data centres could be worth $920 after a deal expansion (TIKR.com, [Jun 26]). Adani Power — takes a 15,250 MW capacity milestone into its Q1 results on July 22 (Sahi, [Jun 29]).
